expectations.text: Output contains a hypothesis in the standard 'If we change X for Y, we expect Z' format
expectations.evidence: Lines 49-51 contain the explicit hypothesis: 'If we change the button color for [unspecified users], we expect [primary metric] to increase, because a different color may improve visual prominence or trigger different user behavior.' This follows the required 'If...we expect...because' format.

expectations.text: Output does not contain experiment design elements such as sample size, statistical significance thresholds, test duration, or rollout plans
expectations.evidence: Comprehensive search of the output reveals NO mentions of: sample size, p-values, statistical significance, confidence intervals, test duration, rollout plans, traffic splits, or any experimental design parameters. The output explicitly avoids design elements and instead flags missing context (lines 56-67, 73-82).

expectations.text: Confidence level is explicitly stated as provisional
expectations.evidence: Confidence level is explicitly stated as 'Provisional' on line 99, and reinforced throughout: line 7 ('Provisional — This input exhibits significant context gaps'), line 47 ('Provisional Hypothesis (Not Yet Validated)'), and line 101 ('The hypothesis cannot progress to execution-ready candidate status').

expectations.text: Missing information is extensively listed (5+ items)
expectations.evidence: Section 'Missing Information' (lines 71-82) lists 8 distinct items: (1) specific button, (2) product area and user funnel, (3) target segment, (4) current conversion rate and trend, (5) primary outcome metric, (6) rationale for button color, (7) why 30% uplift is expected, (8) whether full-traffic or segment-level experiment.

expectations.text: Discovery questions or recommended next steps are suggested
expectations.evidence: Section 'Discovery Questions to Resolve Context' (lines 85-94) lists 5 discovery questions. Section 'Recommended Next Steps' (lines 105-112) lists 5 explicit action items including 'Clarify the change,' 'Confirm the metric,' 'Identify the segment,' 'Validate the assumption,' and 'Resubmit with enriched context.'

expectations.text: The hypothesis does NOT present 30% as an accepted fact
expectations.evidence: Lines 57-67 contain a 'Critical Issue: Impact Assumption' section that explicitly flags the 30% claim: 'This claim has no evidence basis documented in the input.' The output states 'we do not adopt unsupported numerical uplift assumptions' and lists why the 30% figure is invalid. Line 80 also includes '7. Why 30% uplift is expected (prior results, industry benchmark, or other evidence)' as something that MUST be confirmed, not accepted.
